verses.zh: 你们要赞美耶和华！敬畏耶和华，甚喜爱他命令的，这人便为有福！
verses.en: Praise the Lord!How blessed is the one[NOTE:1] who obeys[NOTE:2] the Lord,who takes great delight in keeping his commands.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 112. This wisdom psalm lists some of the benefits of living a godly life. The psalm is an acrostic. After the introductory call to praise, every poetic line (twenty-two in all) begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

Heb “[Oh] the happiness [of] the man.” Hebrew wisdom literature often assumes and reflects the male-oriented perspective of ancient Israelite society. The individual is representative of a larger group, called the “godly” in vv. 3-4. The principle of the psalm is certainly applicable to all people, regardless of their gender. To facilitate modern application, we translate the gender specific “man” with the more neutral “one.” The generic masculine pronoun is used in the following verses.
verses.commentary:
112:1 "Praise the Lord" See note at Ps. 111:1.

▣ "How blessed is the man. . ." This is Wisdom vocabulary.

- blessed (TEV, "happy"), Ps. 112:1 ‒ BDB 80 (cf. Ps. 1:1; 119:1-2)

- blessed, Ps. 112:2 - BDB 138

- well (TEV, "happy"), Ps. 112:5 ‒ BDB 373 II

▣ "fears the Lord" See note at Ps. 111:10.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

▣ "Who greatly delights in His commandments" The VERB (BDB 342, KB 339,
Qal PERFECT) denotes a person's attitude toward YHWH's revelation (cf. Ps. 19:10; 111:2;
119:35). The faithful follower obeys them (cf. Deut. 4:1-2,14,40; 16:12; 30:8,16,19-20; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP).

For "commandments" see the
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

verses.zh: 他的后裔在世必强盛；正直人的后代必要蒙福。
verses.en: His descendants[NOTE:1] will be powerful on the earth;the godly[NOTE:2] will be blessed.
notes: Heb “in his commands he delights very much.” The words “in keeping” are supplied in the translation for clarification. Taking delight in the law is metonymic here for obeying God’s moral will. See Ps 1:2.
verses.commentary:
112:2 From the Ten Commandments we learn that evil moves through generations (cf. Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9,10) but,
praise God, so does faith (cf. Exod. 20:6; Deut. 5:10; 7:9; Exod. 34:7).

112:3a Remember, this is an OT text, the "two ways" of the Mosaic covenant (cf. Leviticus 26;
Deuteronomy 27-28; 30:15-20; Psalm 1; Prov. 4:10-19;
Jer. 21:8; Matt. 7:13-14). This did not work because of mankind's fallen nature (cf. Genesis 3; Romans 1-3; Galatians 3; Hebrews).
Be careful of proof-texting these verses on prosperity as if they were NT promises!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "wealth and riches" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

112:4a This phrase implies that the faithful follower will have understanding amidst the problems of this fallen
age because

- he fears YHWH, Ps. 112:1b,7b

- he delights in His revelation, Ps. 112:1c

- he lives out his faith, Ps. 112:4b-5

- he will not be shaken, Ps. 112:6a

- he does not fear, Ps. 112:8a

▣ The SUBJECT of the VERB "rises" (BDB 280, KB 281, Qal
PERFECT) is unspecified. It could refer to the faithful follower. The UBS Handbook (p. 960)
suggests "He is like a light in darkness, that shines for the honorable (i.e., upright, MASCULINE PLURAL) men."

112:4b These same attributes are said of YHWH in Ps. 111:3b,4b (cf. Exod. 34:6-7). This line of poetry has no
SSUBJECT or VERB but three MASCULINE ADJECTIVES.

- gracious ‒ BDB 337

- merciful ‒ BDB 933

- righteous ‒ BDB 843

It could refer to YHWH (AB, p. 128). NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 204, says that "gracious" is used thirteen times
and always refers to YHWH, except in Ps. 112:4. This implies that Ps. 112:4 might not refer to YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

verses.zh: 他家中有货物，有钱财；他的公义存到永远。
verses.en: His house contains wealth and riches;his integrity endures.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “His seed will be mighty on the earth, the generation of the godly.” The Hebrew term דוֹר (dor, “generation”) could be taken as parallel to “offspring” and translated “posterity,” but the singular more likely refers to the godly as a class. See BDB 189-90 s.v. for other examples where “generation” refers to a class of people.

verses.zh: 正直人在黑暗中，有光向他发现；他有恩惠，有怜悯，有公义。
verses.en: In the darkness a light[NOTE:1] shines for the godly,for each one who is merciful, compassionate, and just.[NOTE:2]
notes: In this context “light” symbolizes divine blessing in its various forms (see v. 2), including material prosperity and stability.

verses.zh: 施恩与人、借贷与人的，这人事情顺利；他被审判的时候要诉明自己的冤。
verses.en: It goes well for the one[NOTE:1] who generously lends moneyand conducts his business honestly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “merciful and compassionate and just.” The Hebrew text has three singular adjectives, which are probably substantival and in apposition to the “godly” (which is plural, however). By switching to the singular, the psalmist focuses on each individual member of the group known as the “godly.” Note how vv. 5-9, like vv. 1-2a, use the singular to describe the representative godly individual who typifies the whole group.

verses.zh: 他永不动摇；义人被记念，直到永远。
verses.en: For he will never be shaken;others will always remember one who is just.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he sustains his matters with justice.”

verses.zh: 他必不怕凶恶的信息；他心坚定，倚靠耶和华。
verses.en: He does not fear bad news.He[NOTE:1] is confident; he trusts in the Lord.
notes: Heb “for an eternal memorial a just [one] will be.”

verses.zh: 他心确定，总不惧怕，直到他看见敌人遭报。
verses.en: His resolve[NOTE:1] is firm; he will not succumb to fearbefore he looks in triumph on his enemies.
notes: Heb “his heart,” viewed here as the seat of the volition and emotions (see Ps 108:1).

verses.zh: 他施舍钱财，周济贫穷；他的仁义存到永远。他的角必被高举，大有荣耀。
verses.en: He generously gives[NOTE:1] to the needy;his integrity endures.[NOTE:2] He will be vindicated and honored.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his heart,” viewed here as the seat of the volition.

verses.zh: 恶人看见便恼恨，必咬牙而消化；恶人的心愿要归灭绝。
verses.en: When the wicked[NOTE:1] see this, they will worry;they will grind their teeth in frustration[NOTE:2] and melt away.The desire of the wicked will perish.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his horn will be lifted up in honor.” The horn of an ox underlies the metaphor (see Deut 33:17; 1 Kgs 22:11; Ps 92:10). The horn of the wild ox is frequently a metaphor for military strength; the idiom “exalt/lift up the horn” signifies military victory (see 1 Sam 2:10; Pss 89:17, 24; 92:10; Lam 2:17).
The Hebrew text uses the singular; the representative wicked individual is in view as typifying the group (note the use of the plural form in v. 10).
Heb “his teeth he will gnash.” In Pss 35:16 and 37:12 this action is associated with a vicious attack.
verses.commentary:
112:10 "gnash his teeth" This was a sign of anger (cf. Ps. 35:16; 37:12; 112:10; Luke 13:28). It also
refers to the experience of judgment (cf. Matt. 8:12; 13:42,50; 22:13; 24:51; 25:30).

▣ "melt away" The wicked will perish (cf. Ps. 68:2). They will melt away in the fire of YHWH's
judgment (cf. Isa. 34:2-4).

Their psychological pain is caused by

- the reversal of their prosperous state

- their exclusion from God's kingdom

- the blessing and prosperity of the faithful followers before their eyes

section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Explain Ps. 112:4a in your own words.

- Do Ps. 112:3,6, and 9 speak of heaven?

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- See Contextual Insights of Psalm 111 for the obvious connections between Psalms 111 and 112.

- Psalm 111 praises YHWH but Psalm 112 praises the faithful follower (cf. Psalm 128).

- he fears the Lord, Ps. 112:1b

- he delights in His revelations, Ps. 112:1c (cf. Ps. 1:2)

- his descendants will be mighty on earth, Ps. 112:2a

- they will be blessed, Ps. 112:2b

- they are prosperous, Ps. 112:3a

- his righteousness endures forever, Ps. 112:3b

- he and his family have light in darkness, Ps. 112:4a

- he is gracious, Ps. 112:4b,5a,9a

- he is compassionate, Ps. 112:4b

- he is upright, Ps. 112:4b

- he conducts his officers with justice, Ps. 112:5b

- he will never be shaken, Ps. 112:6a

- he and his family as righteous people will be remembered forever, Ps. 112:6b

- he will not fear evil tidings, Ps. 112:7a

- his heart is steadfast (cf. Ps. 57:7; 108:1), trusting in the Lord, Ps. 112:7b (cf. Isa. 26:3)

- his heart is steady, BDB 701, KB 759, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE (i.e., by God), Ps. 112:8a

- he will not fear, Ps. 112:8a

- his enemies will be defeated before him, Ps. 112:8b, 10a

- his righteousness endures forever, Ps. 112:9b

- his horn will be exalted in honor, Ps. 112:9c (cf. Ps. 75:10)

- By contrast the wicked will experience the exact opposite. Their fate is specifically mentioned in Ps. 112:10.

- the wicked will see the blessing of the righteous and be vexed

- they will gnash their teeth

- they will melt away

- their desire will perish
